name: Seiko Laurel Alpinist
period: 1959 (launched December 1959 per Sadao Ryugo) - c.1961; end date not documented

mv.notes: Signed 'Seikosha 17 jewels'; dial marked 'Diashock 17J'. No caliber number on the movement per Worn & Wound (for Champion Alpinist) and The Spring Bar. 18,000 vph per Fratello and The Spring Bar. Manufacturing factory (Suwa vs Daini Seikosha) for the Laurel Alpinist not confirmed by a primary source.

cs.crystal: high-domed acrylic
cs.wr: Screw-back 'dust-proof' case; Seiko describes it as highly airtight; Hodinkee Japan says it was called dust-proof (防塵) rather than water-resistant; no rating published
cs.back: Screw-in stainless steel; engraved 'SEIKO LAUREL ALPINIST 14041 STAINLESS STEEL' (per The Spring Bar)
cs.crown: Oversized crown, easy to wind (Fratello; Hodinkee Japan)

strap: Leather strap with a large leather watch pad (cuff) to protect the watch from sweat (Seiko official). Third parties call it a bund-style strap.

msrp.source: 1959 SEIKO NEWS, as cited by HODINKEE Japan (Seiko-sponsored feature); standard Laurel was 3,900 JPY

design: Seiko's first sports watch, per Seiko official pages.
Large wedge-shaped (mountain-shaped) luminous indices at 3, 6, 9 and 12; rectangular indices at the other hours (Seiko; Fratello).
Lume on all indices and on the hour and minute hands (Seiko official).
Dauphine/dagger-style hands; the seconds hand tip has a reddish colour (Fratello).
'Alpinist' script above 6 o'clock. The same logotype appears on later Alpinists (Fratello).
The only Alpinist to carry the Laurel name (Fratello).

Hodinkee Japan (quoting collector Yoshihiko Honda) says it grew out of the Suwa Seikosha Marvel Dust-Proof screw-back model and lumed Laurel variants. The Spring Bar notes Marvel and Champion watches using a 14041 case.
